items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: But talk about this man here, Manuel, I will, I ain't seen him since the time you brought him here. He came by here a year ago. And I sure was glad to see him.

ctx.x: I know. Manuel Mineta teaches all of those same kind of things. Manuel Mineta? He teaches time like that, too, and all that.

I'm talking about Manuel. That is my brother's best friend, him and Freddie. He used to play violin. When Freddie was playing cornet, he used to be, and him and Freddie, every time you see Freddie, you see him. They used to go at this fellow, what they call Henry Morton. Henry Morton's place, they used to go up on Second and Magazine. Well, that was a fine place. Oh, it was a fine place. I don't know if you heard talk about this fellow here, what they call him again, this here fellow, I can't forget it, I can't,…

items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1957-08-04
items.q: He is to play with Freddie. He is to play a violin with Freddie.

ctx.x: Manuel Manetta, that is his best friend.

And that is, he's from over the river. Yes. We know him. He is to play with Freddie. He is to play a violin with Freddie. And so you see, after he started playing the card then, well, he picked the line to it, but he dropped it all. And I had the cornet. He had it here, but I didn't, it then got so old, so I had to do way with it. Because it's the same as my sister, his family. She told it over to me about three weeks ago. And she's been having it ever since he stopped playing it, keeping it for a souvenir. Yes.…
